extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, agents, patent attorneys, and examiners working with the Korean Intellectual Property Office
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory and procedural rules governing who may be a party to patent-related proceedings in Korea and how representation/agency must be established and exercised before the Korean Intellectual Property Office and related tribunals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal capacity to file/participate in patent proceedings (Article 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: No minor under limited guardianship, nor person under adult guardianship, may file an application, request, or conduct any patent-related proceeding unless represented by a legal representative; exception where the minor or person under limited guardianship is able to engage in a legal act independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists examples of acts where an incompetent may act independently (acquiring rights, disposing of permitted property, carrying on special business permitted, representation, making a will, etc.). Note: a minor cannot conduct a patent-related proceeding without consent of a legal representative even when represented by an agent. If discovered during formality examination that proceedings were conducted by an incompetent, examiner shall order amendment; lack of ratification within the designated period invalidates the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unincorporated associations and foundations may act by representative (Article 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A representative or administrator appointed by an unincorporated association or a foundation may act as petitioner requesting examination of a patent application or as petitioner for opposition or trial/retrial in the name of the association/foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although associations without legal personality generally cannot hold rights, where they have a representative/administrator they can be party to limited proceedings (e.g., request for examination, opposition, trial).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent administrator requirement for overseas residents (Article 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: An overseas resident (no domicile/place of business in Korea) may not conduct patent-related proceedings or file legal proceedings against administrative dispositions unless represented by an agent (patent administrator) who has a domicile/place of business in the Republic of Korea, except when the overseas resident sojourns in Korea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent administrator represents the principal in all patent-related proceedings and legal proceedings filed with respect to administrative dispositions within the scope of their authority. If an overseas resident conducts proceedings without designating a patent administrator, examiner shall give opportunity to explain and if not remedied, return documents per Articles 5 and 11 of rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity of foreigners to hold patent rights (Article 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreigners (overseas-resident foreigners) shall not enjoy a patent or rights relating to a patent except where (1) their country allows nationals of the Republic of Korea the same terms, (2) reciprocity/mutuality conditions when Korea allows their nationals similar rights, or (3) where a treaty or equivalent arrangement provides such rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a foreigner has a domicile or place of business in Korea, they shall enjoy patent rights regardless of reciprocity. Notes and case references explain treaty exceptions and how reciprocity/treaty operate in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scope of 'patent-related proceedings'
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent-related proceedings include filing an application (patent, divisional, converted, PCT, etc.), filing requests/petitions (examination, reexamination, trial petitions, technical evaluations, retrial), and other proceedings related to those (accelerated examination, deferral of examination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded are proceedings carried out by the Office against an applicant (notifications, requests), internal examination processing (formality exam, classification, prior art search, substantive exam), proceedings before courts, administrative trials, ordinary public complaints, and certain warnings against third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'incompetents' under Patent Act
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'incompetent' includes (1) persons under age 19 (minors), (2) persons adjudicated to be under limited guardianship due to mental unsoundness, and (3) persons adjudged to be under adult guardianship due to continuous lack of capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An incompetent can only conduct patent-related proceedings through a legal representative except in statutory exceptions. The manual details when a minor or limited-guardian person may act independently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ratification of proceedings conducted by persons lacking capacity (Article 7-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings conducted by a person lacking legal capacity, representation authority, or authorization shall take effect retroactively to the time performed if ratified by the party when they gain legal capacity or authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If formality examination reveals a proceeding was conducted by an incompetent, examiner orders amendment; lack of ratification within specified period leads to invalidation. Retroactive effect upon ratification is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to hold rights by juristic persons
rubrics_metrics.description: A juristic person may obtain rights and obligations independent of members and can be holder of patent rights; when it conducts patent-related proceedings, its name and business address must be stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changing company type (e.g., LLC to corporation) is treated as change of name not change of holder; notification (Annexed Form No.5) must be submitted for change. Discussion also covers effect of rehabilitation/bankruptcy on authority to conduct proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to hold rights by nation and local governments
rubrics_metrics.description: The nation is deemed a juristic person and can be holder of rights. Local governments (as defined by Local Autonomy Act) are deemed juristic persons and can hold rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual notes certain entities (legislative, judicial and administrative branches, government-affiliated organizations, state-run research institutes, universities) are not entitled to be a juristic person and therefore cannot be holders of patent-related rights. Types of local governments that may hold rights are enumerated (Metropolitan City, Province, Si, Gun, Gu, etc.) with jurisdictional limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity of unincorporated associations (detailed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Associations without legal personality generally cannot be patent applicants or holders of rights, but if such an association/foundation has a representative or administrator it may become party to limited proceedings: request for examination, request for technical evaluation on utility models, opposition, trial, retrial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an exception to the general rule of lack of capacity; examiners should check for representative/administrator and the scope of permitted proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of treaties on patent rights and examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Treaties duly concluded and promulgated have the same effect as domestic law; patent treaties to which Korea is a party should be referred to in examination because they may contain more detailed provisions than domestic Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Paris Convention allows priority claims even if first application was for utility model or design; examiners should recognize priority claims accordingly even if domestic law text is narrower.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of power of agent (Article 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: An agent empowered to conduct patent-related proceedings by a principal domiciled/with business in Korea may perform only expressly authorized acts. Enumerated acts include: (1) to convert, abandon or withdraw a patent application; (2) to abandon a patent; (3) to withdraw application for registering extension of patent term; (4) to withdraw a petition; (5) to withdraw a request; (6) to claim or withdraw a priority; (7) to file a petition for trial under Article 132-17; (8) to appoint a sub-agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These acts require express authorization; the provision also applies to patent administrators. Agents must be authorised in writing for these powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of power of agent (Article 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person conducting a patent-related proceeding as an agent (including patent administrators) must prove his/her power in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners check proof of authority (e.g., power of attorney documents); lack of written proof triggers a proposed amendment and may lead to invalidation if not remedied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survival of authority of agent (Article 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority granted to an agent by a principal shall survive notwithstanding events such as: (1) the principal's death or loss of legal capacity; (2) corporate principal's dissolution during merger; (3) termination of principal's duty as trustee; (4) legal representative's death or loss of capacity; (5) termination/change in legal representative's authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority survives these events unless otherwise specified; this affects continuity of representation in ongoing proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of representation (Article 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a principal is represented by two or more agents, each agent shall independently represent the principal before the Commissioner of KIPO or the President of the Trial and Appeal Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each agent can act independently unless specific limitations are provided; examiners and tribunals treat each agent as able to represent the principal separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orders to appoint or replace agents (Article 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commissioner of KIPO or a presiding administrative patent judge finds a person conducting proceedings is unable to properly perform or make statements or is otherwise unfit, they may issue an order to appoint an agent. Similarly they may order replacement of an agent who is unable to perform. They may order a patent attorney to represent the principal and may partially or completely invalidate proceedings conducted before the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a supervisory power to ensure proper representation; orders to appoint/replace may lead to invalidation of prior deficient proceedings. Grounds include inability to perform or make statements in oral hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation for two or more persons (Article 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: When two or more persons jointly perform a patent-related proceeding, each shall represent all, except for particular acts: converting/abandoning/withdrawing an application, withdrawing an application for registering extension of patent term, withdrawing a petition, withdrawing a request, claiming/withdrawing priority, filing petition for trial. If they appoint a representative and notify the Office/Board, only the appointed representative may represent all; appointment must be proved in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proviso requires written proof of appointment. The enumerated exceptional acts require unanimous consent or appointment of a representative to be performed on behalf of all.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of representatives and qualification limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Representatives include legal representatives (empowered by law) and contractual representatives (empowered by principal's intention). Contractual representatives who are not legal representatives may not represent an applicant before KIPO unless they are a patent attorney.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners shall verify representation via Patent Net (patent attorneys' assigned numbers start with '9'); if a person who is neither a patent attorney nor legal representative is appointed, examiner shall propose amendment; unremedied defects result in invalidation. A patent attorney must be registered to act; misuse of title is punishable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent attorney professional and conflict rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent attorney shall engage in representation work at KIPO or courts concerning IP, and shall not handle a case which they previously handled for the other party of the same case; an unregistered patent attorney may not act as such or use the title.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a patent attorney violates conflict or representation prohibitions, an examiner shall order amendment; unremedied deficiencies may invalidate the appointment. Case law examples are cited on interpretation of the prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation, change, and extinguishment of legal representative authority
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle the generation, change and extinguishment of authority for legal representation shall follow the Civil Act. Grounds for extinguishment include death of principal or legal representative, adjudication of incompetency or bankruptcy of legal representative, resignation or removal of guardian. Proceedings may be interrupted when a legal representative dies or loses authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effects of extinguishment/change are not asserted against counterparts unless notified per Civil Procedure Act examples. Practical implications for ongoing patent proceedings (interruption, need for notification) are emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duties regarding representation and attorney verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must check through Patent Net whether a representative is a patent attorney (first figure of assigned number is '9') and confirm legal representatives by certified copies (resident registration or family relation certificate) attached to application; where improper representation is found, propose amendment and treat proceedings conducted by non-qualified persons as invalid if not remedied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical verification steps and documentation requirements are described; failure to remedy leads to invalidation. This entry captures examiner-side procedural checks and remedies.
